'''''Plantago media''''', known as the '''hoary plantain''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the plantain family [[Plantaginaceae]]. It is native to central and western Europe, including Great Britain and introduced to parts of the north-east United States. Its generic name is derived from the [[Latin]] for [[Sole (foot)|sole]]; like other members of the genus ''Plantago'', it should not be confused with the unrelated [[Plantain (cooking)|plantain]], a starchy [[banana]].

==Description==
[[File:Keskmise teelehe õisik Plantago media.jpg|thumb|left|Inflorescence]]
''Plantago media'' grows in damp grassy meadows up to an altitude of {{Convert|2000|m|abbr=on}}. A slender stalk of between {{Convert|5 and 50|cm|4=0|abbr=on}} develops from a basal rosette of finely-haired [[leaf|leaves]]. Delicate pink-white [[flower]]s are borne between May and September. ''P. media'' is [[hermaphrodite]] and is [[pollination|pollinated]] by wind or insects, particularly [[bee]]s.{{citation needed|date=March 2026}}

==Distribution and habitat==
''Plantago media'' is native to Eurasia. It is native to eastern England, but scarce in Scotland and Ireland. It is [[calcicole]], characteristic of soils on chalk or limestone, growing in [[grassland]], meadows, lawns and waste places.<ref name=Blamey>{{cite book|last1=Blamey|first1=M.|last2=Fitter|first2=R.|last3=Fitter|first3=A|year=2003|title=Wild flowers of Britain and Ireland: The Complete Guide to the British and Irish Flora.|publisher=A & C Black|location=London|isbn=978-1408179505}}</ref>{{rp|248}}<ref>Parnell, J. and Curtis, T. 2012. ''Webb's An Irish Flora.'' Cork University Press. {{ISBN|978-185918-4783}}</ref>

==Uses==
The plant is edible. Archeological finds testify to its use{{clarify|reason=for what purpose?|date=August 2018}} during the [[Roman Britain|Roman era in Britain]].<ref>{{cite web | title=''Plantago media''| work=Archaeobotanical Computer Database (ABCD) | url=http://intarch.ac.uk/journal/issue1/tomlinson/scripts/abcd.cfm?taxa=Plantago+media&date=all&action=rec&long=on | accessdate=2006-05-29}}</ref>

100 g of fresh leaves provides 22.586 kcal from 3.33 g protein, 1.99 g net carbohydrates and 0.2 g fat. They are high in fiber with 2.25 g fiber per 100 g.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Guil-Guerrero |first=José Luis |date=August 2010 |title=Nutritional composition of Plantago species (P-major L., P-lanceolata, L., and P-media L.) |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261618820_Nutritional_composition_of_Plantago_species_P-major_L_P-lanceolata_L_and_P-media_L |journal=Ecology of Food and Nutrition |volume=40 |issue=5 |pages=481–495}}</ref>
